corpus_read.note: the corpus this record reads, not a corpus this registration owns: weeks 1-9 plus the Week 10 games settled by official reads. PR-01's own 137/149-game figures are unchanged by anything here

cross_registration_delta_vs_pr01.what_it_measures: the same rule, the same code path, one extra settled game in the corpus. It is not a score and it is not an improvement - it is how sensitive this model is to a single result, which is the thing to know before anyone calls either record a signal

kickoff_offset_applied: US Eastern on standard time for this whole window, i.e. UTC = local + 5h
limits: margin model: no opponent adjustment, personnel, venue, rest or weather inside the rating
total_A is the league average by construction; publishing it is the floor total_B has to beat, not an estimate of any particular game

the Mexico City fixture (Vikings at 49ers) receives the frozen 1.6-point home edge although the official fixture page prints Location MEXICO CITY and Stadium ESTADIO BANORTE; the rule is frozen for this window, so the edge is published as the rule states it and the venue is recorded as a limit, for the next registration to decide on
rest_days columns are published context derived from official schedule dates; the model does not use them in this registration
the settled aggregate has n = 1 and is a demonstration of the mechanism, not a result
read_clock_precision: the reads pack stamps its clock to the minute, so this record could be up to a minute earlier or later than the stamp says. The slack field above is what that uncertainty has to be small against; it is negligible here only because the nearest kickoff is days away, and a record written inside a kickoff minute would have to change this line

settled.reading: n = 1 is not evidence of anything, in either direction. The ledger exists so the number is computed the day an official page prints a final, from the record that was written before it, instead of being reconstructed afterwards.
